inputs.root_cause: Re-read SAL-XLIFF-OBL-130340BC212989D5's own missing_behavior, which judged the 'checked arithmetic' gap as likely non-exploitable (Python's big-int semantics making a dedicated test 'largely redundant'). Rather than trust that judgment at face value, compared directly against the equivalent, already-implemented ubl sibling obligation (SAL-UBL-OBL-8396E06EA0EA75FC) and found its _enforce_tree_limits checks 4 vectors (node count, depth, attribute count, text bytes) while xliff's own version checked only 2 -- a real, previously-unnoticed asymmetry between two structurally-identical readers.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 4 new tests prove: an attribute flood on one element is refused; a document with attributes within the limit loads; a text-byte flood is refused; a document with text within the limit loads.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read SAL-XLIFF-OBL-130340BC212989D5's own missing_behavior text, which characterized the remaining 'checked arithmetic' gap as likely non-exploitable, matching how this session characterized the equivalent ubl/nrrd obligations.

2. Rather than accepting that characterization, read the equivalent already-implemented ubl obligation's own evidence (SAL-UBL-OBL-8396E06EA0EA75FC) and its cited source (ubl's own _enforce_tree_limits) directly, and found it checks FOUR complexity vectors: node count, nesting depth, cumulative attribute count (against max_entries), and cumulative text bytes (against max_decompressed_bytes) -- each checked immediately after being updated during a single stack-based walk.
3. Read xliff's own _enforce_tree_limits directly and found it checks only the first two vectors (node count, nesting depth) -- attribute count and text bytes are never accumulated or checked at all.

4. Confirmed this is a genuine, exploitable gap via direct probing before any fix: constructed a document with 2000 attributes on its root element and loaded it with max_entries=100 explicitly configured -- it sailed straight through unrejected. Repeated with a 5000-byte text node against max_decompressed_bytes=100 -- also sailed through.

5. Extended xliff's _enforce_tree_limits to accumulate and check attribute count and text bytes incrementally during the same walk, matching ubl's exact field choices (max_entries, max_decompressed_bytes) and its 'check immediately after update' discipline precisely, rather than inventing new limit fields or a different check ordering.
6. Re-ran the same 2 probes after the fix: both now correctly raise ResourceLimitError naming the exact limit exceeded. Also confirmed a normal, small document still loads fine with default limits.

7. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (466 tests, zero new fixtures) against the fix to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 466 passed unchanged, confirming no existing fixture happens to exceed the default (generous) attribute/text limits.

8. Wrote 4 formal tests in the existing test_obligation_security_limits.py (extending its established pattern rather than creating a new file, since this obligation's own test infrastructure already lives there), all passing on the first attempt.

9. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (470 passed, was 466, +4), and the full 6-format regression (3436 passed, was 3432, +4; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

10. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-9d90e554533bba95, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

11. Promoted the obligation to implemented: the obligation's own rule_text names 'checked arithmetic for size and count calculations' as a distinct requirement, and all size/count vectors (node count, depth, attribute count, text bytes) are now genuinely bounded, closing a real security gap rather than merely adding a redundant test as the prior tick's own missing_behavior text had assumed was sufficient.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3436 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3432 passed
